title: The Infinitive and the Present Tense
subtitle: Loven, riden, singen — simpler than Old English.
objectives: Master The Infinitive and the Present Tense.
Read and translate authentic Middle English texts.
Prepare for sustained reading in Stage 3.

sections.heading: Content
sections.body: Infinitive ends in -en (loven, riden, singen) or -e (love). Present: I love, thou lovest, he loveth, we loven, ye loven, they loven. The third-person singular -eth (or -th) is the mark of Middle English. Inflection is simpler than Old English but not yet as reduced as modern English.
